**Date:** October 29, 2026  

**To:**  
The Editors-in-Chief  
*Computers & Geosciences*  
Elsevier Science  

**Subject:** Submission of original research paper titled *"A Reproducible Computational Framework for Decoupled Wildfire Ignition and Propagation Benchmarking in the Gran Chaco (2018–2025)"*  

Dear Editors-in-Chief,

Please find enclosed my original research manuscript entitled **"A Reproducible Computational Framework for Decoupled Wildfire Ignition and Propagation Benchmarking in the Gran Chaco (2018–2025): D2 Targets, M3/M2 Inference and an Open Benchmark Against Canadian FWI and INPE"**, which I submit for consideration as a **Research Paper** in *Computers & Geosciences*.

The manuscript presents an auditable computational protocol and reproducible software infrastructure. Its central contribution is the formal D2 target operator, the gated M3/M2 inference policy and the open evaluation harness; the learner is deliberately replaceable.

### Motivation and Core Scientific Novelty
Operational wildfire forecasting in geoscience machine learning frequently suffers from two pervasive methodological pathologies:
1. **Spatial Shortcut Learning:** When models include autoregressive spatial lags without isolating causal mechanisms, gradient-boosted ensembles learn trivial spatial persistence heuristics (*"fire will persist where thermal anomalies already exist"*), resulting in severe false confidence while remaining incapable of anticipating new, spontaneous, or anthropic primary ignitions.
2. **Failure of Canonical Boreal Indices in the Subtropics:** Widely deployed operational frameworks—such as the Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index (FWI) used by EFFIS/GWIS and the CPTEC/INPE Risco de Fogo—consistently fail or invert hazard rankings in water-limited subtropical biomes (e.g., the South American Gran Chaco), where vapor pressure deficit (VPD) and non-linear fuel-curing dynamics govern fire risk.

To address these challenges, I introduce `Incendios_PY`, an open-source computational framework for reproducible decoupled wildfire modeling across **400 006 1-km² grid cells** over an 8-year multi-annual observation baseline (2018–2025). This horizon is anchored to the multi-sensor VIIRS 375 m constellation (Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21), which reduces single-sensor sampling bias across the modeling phases. The framework analytically decouples the operational task into two distinct models: (i) **Multiscale Socio-Ecological Hybrid Ignition** (M3), guided by physics-based monotonic constraints, ecotone edge gradients, and static anthropogenic priors at 10-km and 25-km scales; and (ii) **Tactical Propagation**, driven by a causal spatial contagion kernel at lag t−1.

### Why this Manuscript Fits *Computers & Geosciences*
My work sits precisely at the convergence of **Computer Science Applications** and **Earth and Planetary Sciences**. The computational contribution is the D2 target operator, the gated M3/M2 inference policy and a reusable evaluation harness, released as documented software. The learner is replaceable; the novelty lies in the computational contract.

* **High-Performance Columnar Computational Pipeline:** By integrating Apache Arrow, DuckDB, and Polars, the inference engine processes the entire national territory (400 006 km²) in **~3.47 seconds** on a standard ARM64 machine (~2.21 GB peak RAM), demonstrating that national early-warning systems do not require prohibitive cloud infrastructure.
* **Physics-Guided Machine Learning (PGML):** The framework enforces structural monotonic constraints within LightGBM (+1 for atmospheric dryness and wind pressure, −1 for antecedent rainfall and distance), constraining monotonic responses and reducing counterintuitive artifacts.
* **Spatial and Temporal Control:** The study uses the **D2 target definition** (no t-1 fire within 25 km; no same-cell fire in 10 days) and multi-year out-of-time test partitions (2024–2025). The framework also implements a **50-km spatial block holdout with a 20-km buffer**. Priors are causal (monthly cutoff, rolling 3-year window).
* **Software Engineering and Reproducibility Standards:** The framework is packaged with a complete automated test suite of **76 unit tests** (`tests/`) running in ≈1 minute, verifying algebraic invariants, physical monotonicity, conformal coverage, and spatial KD-Tree queries. All code and workflows are versioned from raw ingestion (`scripts/00_...`) to release and validation outputs (`scripts/34_...`) under the permissive MIT License.
* **Quantitative International Benchmarking:** In retrospective temporal testing over 1 813 966 D2 cell-days during 2024–2025, the hybrid ignition layer M3 achieves a ROC-AUC of **0.8021** in the Gran Chaco and **0.7534** in the Oriental Region, versus **0.5059 / 0.5611** for the full Canadian FWI and **0.5266 / 0.4973** for the INPE. Case-control F0.5 precision is 32.82 % / 30.13 %; after correction to population prevalence (~0.015 % / 0.041 %), operational precision is 0.082 % / 0.198 %. Tactical propagation achieves ROC-AUC **0.9039** (Chaco) and population precision 9.67 %. The 2023 validation selected M3 for temporal nowcasting and M2 as the operational fallback; M1 was rejected as a fallback. These population-adjusted metrics define the operational benchmark.
